CVE-2026-109138.title: Aliro ValidityIteration check bypassed for certificate-trusted Credential Issuer (fail open)
CVE-2026-109138.description:
In the Aliro access control reference
applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA
certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and

authorized holder with an old but correctly issuer-signed Access Document can
be granted physical access after the issuer has advanced its iteration to
revoke that credential. The default Matter provisioning configuration is not
affected. Fixed in v1.2.0.

CVE-2026-126362.title: Astro: Reflected XSS via unescaped slot names in @astrojs/svelte
CVE-2026-126362.description: Astro is a web framework for content-driven websites. CVE-2026-98946.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Disable the V3D interrupt across runtime suspend

vc4_irq_disable() masks the V3D interrupt sources and then calls
synchronize_irq() before the V3D is powered down. However, by itself,
this is not enough to quiesce the interrupt handler.

synchronize_irq() waits for handlers that have already set
IRQD_IRQ_INPROGRESS, and for irqchips reporting IRQCHIP_STATE_ACTIVE.
A GIC interrupt chip is able to mark an interrupt active as soon as a
CPU acknowledges it, so there these checks cover the whole dispatch path.
On RPi 0-3, however, the interrupt controller is ARMCTRL, which has no
active state. A CPU that has read the hwirq out of the pending register
but has not yet reached handle_level_irq() stays invisible to
synchronize_irq().

During a power transition, vc4_irq() may therefore run after the power
domain is off, where every V3D register read will return 0xdeadbeef.
0xdeadbeef has FLDONE, FRDONE and OUTOMEM…

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sched_ext: Fix stall when a task enqueued with SCX_ENQ_LAST lands back on its CPU's local DSQ

With SCX_OPS_ENQ_LAST, the last runnable task on a CPU is passed to
ops.enqueue() instead of being kept running. Exiting tasks without
SCX_OPS_ENQ_EXITING, migration disabled tasks without
SCX_OPS_ENQ_MIGRATION_DISABLED and tasks on an offline rq skip ops.enqueue()
and go straight to the local DSQ. This happens in put_prev_task_scx() after
the pick has settled on idle, so nothing reschedules the CPU, which idles
with the task queued until an unrelated wakeup lands on it or the watchdog

CVE-2026-99444.title: power: supply: sbs-battery: disable polling before supply teardown
CVE-2026-99444.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

power: supply: sbs-battery: disable polling before supply teardown

The managed poll-work cancellation is registered before the power
supply, so cleanup unregisters the supply before draining polling.
A pending or running poller can then call power_supply_changed() on
the released supply.

Commit 8d59cf3887fb ("power: supply: sbs-battery: Fix use-after-free in
power_supply_changed()") moved the IRQ request after supply registration,
but did not change the poll-work cancellation order.

Add a later managed action that disables and drains polling before
supply teardown. Its retained disabled state prevents external-power
callbacks from rearming the poll work after it has been drained.
Keep the original autocancel to initialize work before supply callbacks
can run and to cover failed supply registration.

The teardown ordering issue was found by static analysis.

CVE-2026-99538.title: ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces
CVE-2026-99538.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: ignore network devices of other namespaces

With no interface list configured, ksmbd binds every interface that
comes up. ksmbd_netdev_event() does not look at the device's namespace,
and create_socket() opens the listener in the namespace of the task
raising NETDEV_UP. A container with its own address on a bridge brings
up its interface and finds port 445 in its namespace already taken by
ksmbd, so an SMB server running inside the container fails with
"Address already in use".

Interfaces are also matched by name only, so a container's eth0 going
down would stop the listener on the host's eth0.

Only handle netdev events for devices in init_net.

CVE-2026-99620.title: drm/amdgpu: don't walk the CS chunks when allocating them failed
CVE-2026-99620.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: don't walk the CS chunks when allocating them failed

amdgpu_cs_pass1() sets p->nchunks before allocating p->chunks, and the
allocation failure path skips resetting it. amdgpu_cs_parser_fini() then
frees the kdata of nchunks chunks from a NULL array. On navi48 with the
chunk array allocation failed through failslab:

Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000001: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000008-0x000000000000000f]
RIP: 0010:amdgpu_cs_parser_fini+0x35d/0x710 [amdgpu]
amdgpu_cs_ioctl+0xcae/0x7a20 [amdgpu]
drm_ioctl_kernel+0x180/0x320 [drm]

CVE-2026-99655.title: mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings
CVE-2026-99655.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/memory: reject remote COW faults on PFN mappings

When handling a COW fault without a normal source page (PFN mappings),
__wp_page_copy_user() copies from the faulting user address. For remote
faults, this accesses the wrong address space, resulting in wrong data
getting copied.

For example, user_events updates an enable bit in the registering
process's memory. If that memory needs to be faulted in,
user_event_enabler_fault_fixup() calls fixup_user_fault() from a work
item. Placing the enable bit in a private PFN mapping can trigger this
remote COW path.

Reject these faults with VM_FAULT_SIGBUS when the target mm differs from
current->mm: remote faults. Ordinary (non-PFN) mappings are not affected.

The user-address copy dates back to commit 6aab341e0a28 ("mm: re-architect
the VM_UNPAGED logic"); likely, actual ways to get remote faults in
there on COW PFN mappings appeared afterwards. But the fix is simple…

CVE-2026-99769.title: drm/vc4: Drop the BO reservations outside of job_lock
CVE-2026-99769.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/vc4: Drop the BO reservations outside of job_lock

vc4_queue_submit() calls drm_exec_fini() with job_lock held and interrupts
disabled. Besides unlocking the reservations, drm_exec_fini() frees the
object array with kvfree(), which asks for preemptible task context or a
non-NMI interrupt, and may reach might_sleep() through vfree().

Considering that an array that exceeds a page can take the vmalloc
fallback, call drm_exec_fini() once job_lock is dropped. The reservations
are then held across the job kick, which is harmless as nothing in the
completion path takes a BO reservation.

Note that vc4_attach_fences() has to stay inside the critical section, as
it walks exec, which the job done worker is free to release as soon as
job_lock is dropped.
